## In one paragraph

I'm interested in the problems where a clean dataset, a clear business question and a messy real-world constraint collide. That combination is where my Allied World underwriting work, my BAA1027 Machine Learning research on shopper intent, the EcoEnergy profitability dashboard and my BAA1003 capstone on PriceBeo all sit. Business analytics as a discipline is less about running more models and more about asking the right question, building the evidence carefully, and communicating the result so that a decision can actually be made. That is the lens I want to take into a graduate role.

## How I work

```{=html}
<div class="ab-principles">
  <div class="ab-principle">
    <div class="ab-principle__num">01</div>
    <div class="ab-principle__title">Question before model</div>
    <div class="ab-principle__body">Every analytical project starts with what decision the analysis is supposed to support. My ML research paper concluded that the classification threshold (a decision rule) mattered more than the classifier choice; that finding changed how I think about applied analytics.</div>
  </div>
  <div class="ab-principle">
    <div class="ab-principle__num">02</div>
    <div class="ab-principle__title">Report the negative results</div>
    <div class="ab-principle__body">Two of the three methodological innovations in my research paper did not work. I reported both in the main narrative rather than burying them. Negative results strengthen an argument by locating the positive one more precisely.</div>
  </div>
  <div class="ab-principle">
    <div class="ab-principle__num">03</div>
    <div class="ab-principle__title">Translate, do not summarise</div>
    <div class="ab-principle__body">My CTO role on PriceBeo taught me that translating between technical and commercial teams is not the same as summarising. It means restating trade-offs in the language the other side uses, so that a joint decision can be made.</div>
  </div>
  <div class="ab-principle">
    <div class="ab-principle__num">04</div>
    <div class="ab-principle__title">Discipline scales</div>
    <div class="ab-principle__body">The habits that make competitive bodybuilding work (consistent inputs, honest measurement, long horizons, no shortcuts) are the same habits that make analytical work trustworthy. I try to operate the same way in both.</div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Languages

```{python}
#| label: fig-languages
#| fig-cap: "Language exposure expressed as active years rather than self-rated percentages. English and Polish are both fluent with different domains of use; Spanish is a steadily developing third language."

import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go

languages = pd.DataFrame({
    "Language": ["English", "Polish", "Spanish"],
    "Years":    [18, 22, 4],
    "Level":    ["Fluent · professional", "Fluent · family", "Intermediate"],
    "Context":  ["Education and work in Ireland",
                 "Spoken at home, family in Poland",
                 "Studied through DCU and self-study"],
})

languages = languages.sort_values("Years", ascending=True)

colours = ["#d4a017", "#1e7e34", "#0a579c"]

fig = go.Figure(go.Bar(
    y=languages["Language"],
    x=languages["Years"],
    orientation="h",
    marker=dict(color=colours[:len(languages)]),
    text=[f"{y} years · {lvl}" for y, lvl in zip(languages["Years"], languages["Level"])],
    textposition="outside",
    textfont=dict(size=12, color="#1a1a1a"),
    hovertemplate="<b>%{y}</b><br>Years: %{x}<br>%{customdata}<extra></extra>",
    customdata=languages["Context"],
))

fig.update_layout(
    height=260,
    margin=dict(l=20, r=220, t=10, b=30),
    paper_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)",
    plot_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)",
    font=dict(family="Inter, sans-serif", color="#1a1a1a"),
    xaxis=dict(title="Years of active use", showgrid=True, gridcolor="#eee", range=[0, 28]),
    yaxis=dict(showgrid=False),
    showlegend=False,
)
fig.show()
```

<script>
(function () {
  const sequence = ["ArrowUp", "ArrowUp", "ArrowDown", "ArrowDown",
                    "ArrowLeft", "ArrowRight", "ArrowLeft", "ArrowRight",
                    "b", "a"];
  let position = 0;

  document.addEventListener("keydown", function (event) {
    const key = event.key.length === 1 ? event.key.toLowerCase() : event.key;
    const expected = sequence[position];
    if (key === expected) {
      position += 1;
      if (position === sequence.length) {
        window.open("https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ", "_blank");
        position = 0;
      }
    } else {
      position = key === sequence[0] ? 1 : 0;
    }
  });
})();
</script>
